flox-catalog.description: Versions the Flox catalog can actually resolve, unlike repology's nix_unstable which tracks nixpkgs directly and runs ahead of the flox/nixpkgs snapshots. Only versions built for every system in [options].systems are offered, so a bump cannot break the lock on one system.

flox-catalog-darwin.description: For packages the manifest restricts to aarch64-darwin (aerospace, maccy, container). The all-systems rule yields them zero releases, since they are macOS-only and never build for linux.

customManagers.description: Bump exact version pins resolved across every system in [options].systems. Requiring the pinned value to start with a digit skips the >= floors, which the floor manager below claims instead, and the inline-table pins go/granted (deliberately held). This also matches the darwin-only packages, which the manager below claims as well; the duplicate is suppressed by the packageRule that disables this datasource for them. Renovate compiles custom-manager regexes with RE2, so a negative lookahead is not available to exclude them here.

Bump exact version pins for packages the manifest restricts to aarch64-darwin. Keep this name list in sync with the matchDepNames of the packageRule that disables the all-systems datasource for them, or a package will be offered two conflicting updates.

Dual-catalog packages (claude-code, herdr) exist in both the nixpkgs catalog (bare pkg-path) and the flox catalog (flox/ prefix), and which side tracks upstream faster flips over time; the flox-catalog-lag watchdog (.woodpecker/flox-catalog-lag.yaml) flips pkg-path to the faster side. This manager follows the manifest: packageName is captured from the pkg-path line, so a flip needs no renovate.json edit. The all-systems manager above still matches these version lines under the bare key, which queries the nixpkgs name regardless of pkg-path; the -pin depName suffix here is what lets the packageRule below disable those duplicates without also disabling these -- on the nixpkgs side the two deps share a packageName, so depName is the only discriminator. RE2 has no backreferences to tie the key across lines, so each package's block must stay contiguous and in pkg-path/pkg-group/version order or the manager silently stops matching it.

Bump the >= floors in place. These are a forward ratchet rather than real minimum requirements, and left to drift by hand they silently encode whenever they were last touched -- the toplevel floors sat on 2025-08 versions for a year. Only the numeric part is captured, so the >= survives the rewrite and the constraint stays a floor instead of becoming an exact pin. That distinction is load-bearing: every floored package shares the toplevel group, and 17 independently-bumped exact pins in one group is exactly the 'constraints too tight' failure the manifest header warns about, whereas any number of open-ended floors can be satisfied by a single snapshot indefinitely. The char class allows a leading underscore for _1password-cli.
Bump zap flake ref to the latest tagged release

packageRules.description: Approve-to-merge: arm Forgejo's scheduled merge on every non-major PR. Forgejo holds it until branch protection is satisfied (one approval + the validate status), then rebases onto current main and merges. The Flox lock is not part of the PR: it is regenerated on main after merge by flox-relock.yaml. Majors are left unarmed and merged by hand. automergeStrategy rebase maps to Forgejo's rebase-merge, which the repo must allow (kubernetes/cicd/forgejo/tf in the homelab repo manages that): Forgejo checks the style only when the merge fires, so a disallowed one arms fine and then never merges. Only PRs created after this lands are armed.

Keep the renovate-validate pipeline image in step with the CronJob pinned in devops-blocks (kubernetes/cicd/renovate/manifests/base/kustomization.yaml), so the validator never accepts config the deployed bot rejects. Upstream ships ~6 releases/day, so batch to one PR per week and let releases settle. timestamp-optional keeps the rule fail-open if the docker datasource cannot resolve a releaseTimestamp, which would otherwise block the bump indefinitely.
The woodpecker manager is enabled only to track the pinned renovate validator image. The other pipeline images are floating (plugin-git is untagged, flox is :latest), so they yield no updates.

Retained from the repology era so a failed flox-relock check still gets retried. The flox-catalog datasources only offer resolvable versions, so this should become unnecessary; drop it after a few clean runs.

Darwin-only packages are matched by both custom managers, since RE2 gives the all-systems manager no way to exclude them. Disabling the all-systems datasource for them leaves the flox-catalog-darwin result as the only update source.

The dual-catalog packages are matched twice: by the all-systems manager (depName = bare key, packageName = bare key, i.e. always the nixpkgs entry) and by their dedicated manager (depName = key-pin, packageName from pkg-path). Disable the bare-key duplicates. Matching on depName rather than packageName is what keeps this correct on both sides of a catalog flip: with the package on the nixpkgs side both deps carry the same packageName, and a packageName match would disable them both.
aerospace has never cut a stable release; every catalog version is a -Beta prerelease. Without this Renovate finds no valid target and silently never opens a PR.
halloy versions are YYYY.M with an optional patch (2026.7, 2026.7.2), plus one legacy 23.1-alpha1. Not strict semver, but loose orders them correctly.

nmap ships two-component versions (7.99), which strict semver rejects outright -- same shape as halloy, same fix. Needed now that the >= floors are Renovate-managed. Do not widen this to the floored packages as a group: zoxide's catalog still carries a legacy 2023-11-20 entry that loose ranks above 0.10.0 and would offer as a downgrade, the same trap documented for wezterm above. Strict semver skips it, so every other floor is left on the default.

wezterm currently tags YYYY-MM-DD but the catalog still carries 12 legacy YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-hash versions. Under loose, 20240203 > 2026, so Renovate would propose a downgrade. This regex versioning matches only the current format, which makes the legacy versions invalid and therefore skipped.
